examples.en: The school holds an entrance ceremony every spring.
We held a quiet wedding with just family.
City hall will hold a commemoration ceremony tomorrow.
It is the day the company holds its founding anniversary ceremony.

examples.ko: 비가 와도 예정대로 행사를 거행하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to hold the event as planned even if it rains.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들이 모여 제사를 거행하고 돌아갔어요.
examples.en: The villagers gathered, held the memorial rite, and went home.

explain: '식을 하다'보다 격식 있는 표현이라 '식', '행사', '의식' 앞에서만 써요. 파티나 모임에는 어색해서 '열다'를 써요.
explain_en: This is more formal than 식을 하다 and is used only with words like 식, 행사 and 의식. It sounds odd with a party or a casual meeting, where 열다 is used.

examples.ko: 어머니가 콩가루를 묻힌 경단을 만들어 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mother made me gyeongdan coated with bean powder.
Gyeongdan is chewy and sweet, so it makes a good snack.

examples.ko: 시장에서 색깔이 예쁜 경단을 한 팩 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a pack of pretty-colored gyeongdan at the market.

examples.ko: 경단이 너무 쫀득해서 계속 먹게 돼요.
examples.en: The gyeongdan is so chewy that I keep eating it.

examples.ko: 명절에는 경단 모양을 예쁘게 빚어 봐요.
examples.en: On holidays, we try shaping gyeongdan nicely.
I put gyeongdan in a cold fruit punch and ate it.

explain: 영어로 딱 맞는 말이 없어서 'rice cake ball'처럼 설명하곤 해요. '송편, 인절미'처럼 떡 이야기에서 나오고, 화채에 넣어 먹기도 해요.
explain_en: There is no exact English word, so people describe it as a 'rice cake ball'. It comes up in talk about rice cakes like '송편' and '인절미', and it can also be added to 화채 (fruit punch).

examples.ko: 강아지에게 한 달에 한 번 구충제를 먹여요.
examples.en: I give my puppy a dewormer once a month.
The vet said to give the dewormer regularly.

examples.ko: 이 구충제가 우리 고양이에게도 맞는지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I'm not sure this dewormer is right for my cat too.
The dewormer made my stomach a little upset.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 학교에서 나눠 준 구충제도 생각나요.
examples.en: I also remember the dewormer pills they handed out at school when I was little.
I asked at the pharmacy about dewormers.

explain: 몸속 기생충을 없애는 약이고, 반려동물 이야기에서 특히 자주 나와요. 일상에서 '기생충약'이라고도 말해요. 약은 보통 '먹이다'(동물에게)와 '먹다'(사람이)를 구분해서 써요.
explain_en: It is medicine that gets rid of parasites inside the body, and it comes up especially often in talk about pets. In daily speech people also say '기생충약'. Note the pair '먹이다' (give to an animal) and '먹다' (take yourself).

examples.ko: 할머니는 평생 모은 책을 도서관에 기증했어요.
examples.en: My grandmother donated the books she collected over her lifetime to the library.

examples.ko: 저는 안 입는 옷을 복지관에 기증해요.
examples.en: I donate clothes I no longer wear to the welfare center.
I signed a form to donate my organs.

examples.ko: 작가가 그림을 학교에 기증해서 복도에 걸렸어요.
examples.en: The artist donated a painting to the school, and it was hung in the hallway.
Please wipe the items you will donate clean and bring them.
After donating, my heart felt lighter.

explain: '기부하다'는 주로 돈을 내는 일이고, 기증하다는 책, 옷, 작품, 장기 같은 물건이나 몸의 일부를 주는 일에 써요. 돈은 '기부', 물건은 '기증'이라고 구별하면 쉬워요. '~에 기증하다'로 받는 곳을 말해요.
explain_en: 기부하다 is mostly about giving money, while 기증하다 is for giving things like books, clothes, artworks, or body parts such as organs. It helps to remember 기부 for money and 기증 for items. The receiving place goes with 에, as in '~에 기증하다'.

en: to promise; to assure; to pledge

examples.en: I resolved to start exercising this year for sure.
I promised my teacher I would never be late again.
He vowed in his heart never to give up.

examples.ko: 새해에는 일찍 일어나기로 다짐하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people resolve to get up early in the new year.
My friend and I pledged to each other to work hard.

examples.ko: 다짐한 대로 매일 한국어를 공부하고 있어요.
examples.en: As I resolved, I study Korean every day.

explain: 스스로에게나 남에게 꼭 하겠다고 마음을 굳게 먹을 때 써요. '결심하다'와 비슷한데, '다짐하다'는 한 번 더 확인하듯 말하는 느낌이 있어요. 보통 '-겠다고 다짐하다', '-기로 다짐하다' 형태로 써요.
explain_en: Used when firmly making up your mind, to yourself or to others. It is close to '결심하다', but '다짐하다' has the feel of reaffirming. It is typically used in the forms '-겠다고 다짐하다' and '-기로 다짐하다'.

examples.ko: 새해에는 우리 가족 모두 만사형통하길 빌어요.
examples.en: I wish that everything goes well for our whole family this new year.
Passing the exam doesn't mean everything will go smoothly.

examples.ko: 모든 일이 늘 만사형통일 수는 없어요.
examples.en: Not everything can always go perfectly.

examples.ko: 친구가 개업 선물로 만사형통이라고 쓴 액자를 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend gave me a frame that says 'may all go well' as a shop-opening gift.

examples.ko: 친구에게 새해 문자로 만사형통을 빌어 줬어요.
examples.en: I wished my friend good fortune in everything with a New Year text.
Boss, I hope everything you do goes well again this year!

explain: 모든 일이 잘되기를 비는 덕담이라 새해 인사나 개업 선물 문구에서 많이 보여요. 평소 대화에서는 '다 잘될 거예요'처럼 말해요. 보통 소망을 말할 때 쓰고, 지금 상황을 설명할 때는 드물어요.
explain_en: It is a well-wishing phrase, often seen in New Year greetings and shop-opening gifts. In everyday talk people say '다 잘될 거예요' instead. It is mostly used to express a wish and rarely to describe a current situation.

examples.ko: 오월에는 온 마을이 논에서 모내느라 바빠요.
examples.en: In May the whole village is busy transplanting rice in the paddies.
It rained, so we couldn't transplant the rice today.
My father went out to the paddy and transplanted rice from the morning.

examples.ko: 기계로 모내면 일이 훨씬 빨리 끝나요.
examples.en: If you transplant by machine, the work finishes much faster.
You have to transplant after filling the paddy with water.
This year the villagers transplanted the rice together.

explain: 논에 모를 옮겨 심는다는 뜻으로, 농사 이야기에서 써요. 일상에서는 이 동사보다 명사 '모내기'를 써서 '모내기를 하다'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요. '모를 내다'처럼 띄어 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used in farming talk for planting seedlings in the paddy. In daily speech, people more often use the noun '모내기' and say '모내기를 하다'. It is also written separately as '모를 내다'.

en: invigoration of the body; nurturing of the body

examples.en: On the hottest days of summer, we boost our health with samgyetang.
The exams are over, so I went with my family to eat something restorative.
What is good for building up your strength?
My father had herbal medicine made for me so that I could build up my health.
I have no energy lately, so I need something to build me up.
I ate eel to build up my strength and now I feel energetic.

explain: 기운이 없거나 더울 때 영양가 있는 음식을 먹어서 몸을 챙기는 것을 말해요. 보통 '몸보신하다'나 '몸보신을 하다'로 쓰고, 삼계탕 같은 '보양식'과 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means taking care of your body by eating nourishing food when you feel weak or in the summer heat. It is used as '몸보신하다' or '몸보신을 하다' and often appears together with '보양식' (health food) such as samgyetang.

examples.en: The lunch duty students serve the lunch.
Volunteers served warm meals for free.

examples.ko: 학교에서는 아이들이 줄을 서면 선생님이 배식하세요.
examples.en: At school, when the kids line up, the teacher serves the food.
Today is my day to serve the food.
Serving time at the cafeteria starts at twelve.

examples.ko: 다 같이 줄을 서서 순서대로 배식했어요.
examples.en: We all lined up and got served in order.

explain: 급식, 무료 급식, 군대 식당처럼 많은 사람에게 음식을 차례로 나눠 줄 때 써요. 식당에서 손님에게 음식을 가져다주는 것에는 '서빙하다'나 '내오다'가 어울려요. 음식을 받는 쪽은 '배식을 받다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when food is handed out in turn to many people, such as school meals, free meals or a barracks mess hall. For bringing food to customers in a restaurant, '서빙하다' or '내오다' fits better. The person receiving food says '배식을 받다'.

en: official tour of several places or countries

examples.ko: 대통령이 다음 주에 유럽 순방을 떠나요.
examples.en: The president leaves on a tour of Europe next week.

examples.ko: 이번 순방에서 여러 나라와 협정을 맺었어요.
examples.en: On this tour they signed agreements with several countries.
The prime minister's tour schedule was on the news.

examples.ko: 순방이 끝나면 곧 국내 일정을 시작해요.
examples.en: When the tour ends, they start the domestic schedule soon.
On the tour, the delegation also visited local schools.

examples.ko: 이번 순방의 가장 큰 성과는 무엇인가요?
examples.en: What is the biggest result of this tour?

explain: 여러 나라나 지역을 차례로 방문하는 일이에요. 한 곳만 가면 '방문'이라고 해요. 주로 대통령, 총리, 장관 같은 사람의 일정에 쓰고 일반 여행에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It means visiting several countries or regions in turn. Going to just one place is '방문'. It is mainly used for the schedules of figures like the president, prime minister or ministers, not for ordinary trips.

examples.ko: 저는 현장에 가기 전에 안전모와 안전화를 챙겼어요.
examples.en: Before going to the site, I packed a hard hat and safety shoes.
You must wear safety shoes at a construction site.
The safety shoes were heavy, so walking was hard at first.

examples.ko: 새 안전화를 사려고 작업복 가게에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to a workwear shop to buy new safety shoes.
My father tied his safety shoe laces tightly.

examples.ko: 안전화 앞부분이 단단해서 발을 보호해 줘요.
examples.en: The front of safety shoes is hard, so they protect your feet.

explain: 공사장이나 공장에서 발을 다치지 않게 신는 작업용 신발이에요. 보통 '안전모'와 같이 말하고, 동사는 '신다'를 써요. 일반 운동화와는 달리 일할 때 꼭 필요한 장비로 생각해요.
explain_en: These are work shoes worn at construction sites or factories to protect your feet. It is often mentioned together with '안전모' (hard hat), and the verb is '신다' (to wear on the feet). Unlike regular sneakers, they are seen as required gear for work.

examples.ko: 조리대 위에 칼과 도마를 올려 두었어요.
examples.en: I put the knife and cutting board on the counter.
The counter is narrow, so cooking is inconvenient.
When I finish cooking, I wipe the counter clean.

examples.ko: 조리대는 늘 정리해 두는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It is best to keep the counter tidy at all times.
I lined the vegetables up on the counter.
The space between the counter and the sink is too narrow.

explain: 음식을 썰고 만드는 작업 공간이에요. '싱크대'는 설거지하는 쪽을 말할 때가 많아서 '조리대'와 구분해서 쓰기도 해요. 집에서는 '싱크대 옆 작업대'처럼 풀어서 말해도 돼요.
explain_en: It is the work surface where you cut and prepare food. '싱크대' often refers to the washing side, so people sometimes separate it from '조리대'. At home you can also just say something like '싱크대 옆 작업대'.

examples.en: I chatted with my friend all night.

examples.ko: 저는 해외에 사는 가족과 자주 채팅해요.
examples.en: I often chat with my family living abroad.
You shouldn't chat during class.
I missed the bus while chatting.

examples.ko: 새로 알게 된 친구와 채팅하는 중이에요.
examples.en: I'm chatting with a friend I just met.

examples.ko: 오늘은 시간이 없어서 길게 채팅할 수 없어요.
examples.en: I don't have time today, so I can't chat for long.

explain: 요즘은 '채팅하다'보다 '톡하다', '카톡하다', '메시지 보내다'를 더 자주 말해요. '채팅'은 인터넷에서 글자로 실시간으로 이야기하는 것이고, 목소리로 하면 '통화하다'예요.
explain_en: These days '톡하다', '카톡하다' or '메시지 보내다' are more common than '채팅하다'. Chatting means typing back and forth in real time online; by voice it is '통화하다'.

examples.en: Farmers sow seeds in the spring.
We sowed the barley before the rain came.

examples.ko: 올해는 날씨가 추워서 파종하는 시기를 늦췄어요.
examples.en: It was cold this year, so we delayed the sowing time.
After plowing the field, you just sow the seeds.
Grandfather harvested the beans he had sown himself.

examples.ko: 상추를 파종하려면 흙을 먼저 부드럽게 해야 해요.
examples.en: To sow lettuce, you first have to loosen the soil.

explain: 일상에서는 '씨를 뿌리다'라고 하고, '파종하다'는 농업이나 교과서, 뉴스에서 많이 나와요. 이미 자란 어린 식물을 옮겨 심는 것은 '모종을 심다'라고 해서 달라요.
explain_en: In daily speech people say '씨를 뿌리다', while '파종하다' appears in farming contexts, textbooks and news. Moving an already-grown seedling is '모종을 심다', which is different.

examples.en: I went to donate blood during vacation.

examples.ko: 저는 두 달에 한 번 헌혈해요.
examples.en: I donate blood once every two months.
After donating blood, I got a snack.

examples.ko: 몸이 안 좋으면 헌혈할 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't donate blood if you feel unwell.
They give a souvenir to people who donated blood.
I was a little nervous the first time I donated blood.

explain: '피를 주다'라고 하지 않고 '헌혈하다'라고 말하고, 명사로 '헌혈을 하다'라고도 해요. 헌혈하는 곳은 '헌혈의 집'이라는 이름이 많아요. 피를 받는 쪽은 '수혈을 받다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Koreans say '헌혈하다' rather than 'give blood', and also use the noun in '헌혈을 하다'. Donation places are often named '헌혈의 집'. The person who receives the blood is said to '수혈을 받다'.
